problem: "Every electric field is this law added up over all charges" is too broad: an electric field also arises from a changing magnetic field, which Coulomb's law does not cover. A student could carry the wrong generalisation out of the electrostatics unit.
fix: "Every electrostatic field is this law added up over all charges."

problem: "The constant 1/(4πε₀) equals 9×10⁹ N m² C⁻²" states an exact equality; the accepted value is 8.99×10⁹, rounded here to one significant figure.
fix: "The constant 1/(4πε₀) is approximately 9×10⁹ N m² C⁻² (more exactly 8.99×10⁹), and ε₀ = 8.854×10⁻¹² C² N⁻¹ m⁻²."

problem: The point-charge field is printed as "E = (1/(4πε₀)) Q / r² r̂", which can be misread as Q divided by (r²r̂).
fix: Write it as E = (1/(4πε₀)) (Q/r²) r̂, with the bracket making clear that r̂ only gives the direction.

problem: "The number of lines through unit area shows the field strength" is loose: the count must be per unit area drawn perpendicular to the lines, otherwise a tilted area gives a wrong idea of the field.
fix: "The number of lines crossing unit area perpendicular to the lines is proportional to the field strength."

problem: The same remark about Gauss's law being quicker for symmetric distributions appears at the end of both sections; the repetition adds nothing.
fix: Keep it once, at the end of Section 3 where Gauss's law is introduced by name.
